Leo (customer): Hey team, hitting a weird one on embeddings endpoint after switching to an int8 quantization profile. Previously we used `embedding-v3-fp16` and got 512-d vectors. After switching to `embedding-v3-int8` we now get length 384 vectors. Did something change in the model catalog? Also throughput dropped even with batching enabled. Anyone seen this? :confused:

Maya (support): Sorry you're seeing that, Leo. Can you paste the exact request you sent (sanitized token ok) and a response sample? Also please include the request_id from the response headers if available.

Leo (customer): Yep, sanitized curl below and response snippet. request-id: `req_01G7Z9XK8M`.

```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"embedding-v3-int8","input":"The quick brown fox"}'
```

Response (trimmed):

```
{"object":"embedding","model":"embedding-v3-int8","data":[{"embedding":[0.012,0.003,...],"index":0}]}
```

Length of `embedding` array = 384. We also tried batching with header `X-Redwood-Batch-Size: 8` and saw throughput drop and some 502s.

Sam (support-engineer): Thanks, Leo. Two quick sanity checks: 1) can you confirm you didn't accidentally request a different model id (sometimes catalog names changed); 2) can you try the same input with `embedding-v3-fp16` to confirm dims go back to 512?

Leo (customer): Confirmed — `embedding-v3-fp16` returns 512. We explicitly passed `embedding-v3-int8`. We expected identical dim, just different precision.

Maya (support): Copying eng-ml. Tagging Jordan. Jordan — any known model packaging changes that could change embedding dimension when you quantize?

Jordan (eng-ml): Not expected behavior. Quantization (fp16 -> int8) should not change output embedding dimensionality. Two possibilities: 1) the `embedding-v3-int8` variant is actually a different backbone (e.g., v3-small) with 384-d head, or 2) the runtime selected a fallback compatible model at request time because of kernel availability, and that fallback has 384-d.

Jordan (eng-ml): Can you share the full response headers and the model hash/version? Also, if you have the server-side `x-redwood-selected-variant` header it would help.

Leo (customer): Headers pasted: `x-request-id: req_01G7Z9XK8M`, `x-redwood-selected-variant: embedding-v3-int8`, `x-redwood-model-hash: sha256:ab12...`, `x-runtime-kernel: cudnn-8.3`.

Sam (support-engineer): Hmm we see selected-variant matches. Two more things to repro from your side: 1) include `?debug=true` query so runtime returns dimension metadata, and 2) try setting `precision":"fp16"` in the body to force fp16 runtime path (workaround). Example below.

```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?debug=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"embedding-v3-int8","input":"The quick brown fox","precision":"fp16"}'
```

Jordan (eng-ml): Adding more context: In our packaging pipeline we create distinct artifacts for quantized variants. There was a recent optimization PR that tried to merge small/medium heads for int8 builds to reduce footprint on constrained GPUs — that could accidentally change head dims if a wrong config file was used during packaging. I'm going to look at the packaging job for `embedding-v3-int8` and compare the head config to `embedding-v3-fp16`.

EngBot: Noted. Escalation created: INC-2026-347. Assigned to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

Maya (support): While Jordan investigates, Leo — for immediate unblock can you: 1) use the explicit fp16 variant (`embedding-v3-fp16`) to get 512-d vectors; 2) avoid the int8 variant for now if downstream math expects 512 dims; 3) if you need the int8 latency/cost benefits, we can spin a dedicated int8 artifact build for your account (request via support ticket).

Leo (customer): Ok thanks. Could you also explain why batching worsened throughput? We turned on `X-Redwood-Batch-Size: 8` expecting higher TP. Instead it's slower and sometimes 502.

Sam (support-engineer): Likely related: if the model variant is smaller (384-d) the runtime's kernel selection may choose a different CUDA path. Also if the quantized runtime uses a different memory layout it can reduce concurrency. The 502s look like timeouts under the load balancer because some nodes hit higher latency with large batches. We need logs from the affected request ids to confirm. Can you share a short time window (timestamps) when you saw the 502s?

Leo (customer): 2026-02-12T21:14:03Z through 21:18:00Z. We saw ~8 errors.

Jordan (eng-ml): I'll correlate packaging and runtime logs. Initial quick findings: packaging PR #4421 may have swapped `embedding_head_size` for some int8 builds — that exactly explains 384 vs 512. If true it's a packaging-time bug, not a runtime routing issue.

Jordan (eng-ml): Short term workaround: request the FP16 model; alternative: use `model:"embedding-v3-int8-fixed-512"` if we can build it. I'll coordinate with runtime to add a temporary alias if needed.

Maya (support): Created a support ticket to request an urgent rebuild: TKT-8891. ETA request: can you provide priority and if you require a backfilled dataset to repro outside your account?

Leo (customer): Priority high — this breaks our similarity indexing pipeline. We can provide a small repro dataset.

Jordan (eng-ml): Re: batching slowdown — two notes: 1) if different kernels are used for int8 path some of them do not support fused multi-request execution so we end up executing requests sequentially under the same batch window (worse throughput), 2) quantized kernels sometimes add dequant->compute->requant steps that offset batching wins for short sequences. We'll investigate kernel selection logs and provide a writeup.

Sam (support-engineer): For support repro please run this script (sanitized) and paste the `x-request-id` for failing calls so we can pull node logs.

```
python repro_emb.py --model embedding-v3-int8 --batch-size 8 --inputs example.json
# repro_emb.py prints per-call request ids
```

Leo (customer): Running it now. Will paste ids in a minute. :eyes:

[10 minutes later]

Leo (customer): Pasted request ids in the ticket: req_01G7Z9XK8M, req_01G7Z9YB2P, req_01G7Z9ZQ1A. Also I see this in the response with debug=true:

```
{"model":"embedding-v3-int8","embedding_dim":384,"precision":"int8","backend":"tvm","batching":"adaptive"}
```

Jordan (eng-ml): Confirms packaging mismatch. I'm pulling the build artifact now. Looks like a config file in the quantization pipeline referenced `head_dim: 384` by mistake for a subset of int8 builds. Creating a hotfix to repackage with `head_dim: 512`. If CI passes we can push a replacement artifact tonight.

EngBot: INC-2026-347 status update: eng-ml investigating packaging configs. Target fix window: 6 hours.

Maya (support): Will update the ticket with the workaround (use `embedding-v3-fp16`) and the provisional ETA. Leo — thanks for the repro data. We'll keep you posted. :thumbsup:

Leo (customer): Great — appreciate the quick turnaround. One last question: will using fp16 preserve the same cosine similarity behavior as int8? We noticed small shifts in similarity scores between fp16 and int8 in other contexts.

Jordan (eng-ml): Good question. Quantization can slightly change floating point arithmetic and thus embedding values; small delta is expected. But switching back to the correct dimensionality is the main priority. After repackaging we'll run regression evals on a held-out similarity set (we'll attach the metrics to the ticket). If you need exact bit-for-bit reproducibility, use the same model artifact + precision in production.

Maya (support): Closing loop: ticket TKT-8891 created, escalation INC-2026-347 open. Workarounds: use `embedding-v3-fp16` or request a rebuild. ETA provisional: 6 hours for hotfix; we'll update if it slips.

Sam (support-engineer): Follow-ups for eng-runtime: please verify that the runtime doesn't silently select a different backbone when quantized and ensure debug headers include `x-redwood-build-config`. Jordan — can you post CI job number once packaging fix is pushed?

Jordan (eng-ml): Will do. CI job #87654 will contain the corrected artifact if green.

Leo (customer): Thanks all. Leaving this open until the hotfix is in.

Maya (support): Will keep thread active until fixed. :eyes:
